title: One Agent API response, parsed in three languages
pins: What ONE Agent API response body becomes for the caller. Three decisions ride on it that a consumer cannot make for itself: whether the run is FINISHED, which is what the polling loop turns on; which CITATIONS it carries and in what order, because a UI numbers them and the answer text refers to them by that number; and whether the body is REFUSED at all and under which identifier, because a consumer switches on that identifier to tell a bad request from a rate limit from an unreadable body. The body is UNTRUSTED input -- it is whatever the provider sent -- so the malformed rows are not hypothetical shapes but the ones a parser is most likely to disagree about.
scope: Parse one Agent API response through retrieve (legacy default), cancel, or create. Cancellation-only response_id presence, exact requested-ID binding, cancelling classification and optional incomplete_details.reason projection are covered. Bounded polling is tested in each client package, not by this single-response corpus.
construction: Every row is execution output from the real reference and port clients against stubbed transports. The original seventeen retrieve rows and every original parsed value are unchanged. Twenty-eight new rows exercise cancel-only response_id presence/precedence and exact requested-ID correlation, create/retrieve alias isolation, cancelling parser tolerance, incomplete-reason values, and HTTP refusal. New PHP goldens were measured from candidate reference source; fresh normal released-artifact reproduction is a separate release gate. JSON object/list containers are preserved by the generator.
findings: 1 of forty-five rows agree across all three languages; both ports agree on all forty-five. All twenty-eight new independent lifecycle expectations pass in each language. The original seventeen rows and their known G-29 through G-32 divergences remain unchanged. A synthetic cancelling GET row is parser tolerance, not evidence of a provider response. Bounded polling, raw preservation, exact opaque-ID privacy, one-POST/no-retry and retrieve() recovery guidance have separate native package regressions. What differs: (1) G-29, an empty `usage` is `[]` in the reference and `{}` in both ports -- a second instance of G-20; (2) G-30, the refusal identifier has a different SHAPE, not just a different name -- the reference has no machine-readable code and puts its own client identifier in the slot the ports reserve for the provider's error type; (3) G-31, a JSON ARRAY body is `invalid_response` in the reference and `unreadable_response` in the ports, and the ports are right; (4) G-32, a numeric-string `created_at` is coerced by the reference and nulled by both ports.
